data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004's mechanism (linear/additive checklist weighting vs non-linear expert pattern recognition) is asserted but not causally connected to the verifiable-outcome comparison the problem frames. It claims any perceived gain is from 'simple task-decomposition that ignores systemic edge cases,' yet provides no mechanism showing that the ignored interactions are causally responsible for enough errors to make the panel worse ON AVERAGE than the expert. The problem asks for evidence within a single evaluation that distinguishes genuine gain from compliance-tracking; SRC_004 gives no evaluation-level causal test—it only restates that checklists are linear and experts are non-linear. Without a specified mechanism by which interaction effects produce verifiable errors AND an evidentiary trace that would reveal those errors in one evaluation, the causal claim is incomplete.
